title: ICE Agent at NYC Shooting Has History of Alleged Violence and Illegal Arrests
gist: WIRED identifies ICE supervisor Brenden Cuni, seen brandishing a rifle at a Manhattan shooting where agents shot Oscar Belgal with a 5-year-old in the car, as an agent repeatedly accused in federal court of violent and unlawful arrests, with judges finding a 'fraudulent' warrant and video contradicting his sworn account. The piece also shows ICE's Mobile Fortify face-recognition app being used to justify an arrest despite records showing a work permit.

insights.claim: ICE agents shot Oscar Belgal in Manhattan's Marble Hill neighborhood after surrounding his car, in which a 5-year-old child was sitting, firing as many as seven rounds according to witnesses; Belgal was hospitalized with a reported neck wound.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Escalating ICE use-of-force incidents in major cities heighten political and legal friction over immigration enforcement.

insights.claim: WIRED identifies the agent brandishing a modified AR-15-style rifle at the scene as Brenden Cuni, a supervisor on ICE's National Fugitive Operations team who also worked Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Accountability scrutiny of individual agents is intensifying.

themes.theme: Judicial findings of unlawful ICE arrests

insights.claim: Federal judges have repeatedly found arrests involving Cuni unlawful: one called a warrant he signed 'fraudulent', another said video contradicts his sworn account, and in a third case the government withdrew his sworn statements as inaccurate.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Mounting adverse rulings increase litigation exposure and constrain ICE street-arrest tactics.
insights.quote: One judge called an arrest warrant he signed “fraudulent,” while another said that video evidence contradicts his sworn account of an arrest
insights.locator: A WIRED review of federal court cases

insights.claim: Judge Gary Brown found Cuni searched five databases for a Bronx man, found nothing, then signed a warrant saying searches confirmed he was undocumented; ICE later added the man to those databases to create the missing record.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Shows data-integrity problems in ICE enforcement databases, relevant to vendors supplying them.
insights.locator: In at least three federal cases this year

insights.claim: Judge Brian Cogan ruled an arrest unlawful after doorbell footage contradicted Cuni's account; Cuni had used ICE's Mobile Fortify face-recognition app, which showed no lawful-entry record but did show a federal work permit, and treated the missing entry record as evidence the man was undocumented.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Illustrates risks of acting on face-recognition/database lookups in enforcement, a liability issue for surveillance-tech deployments.

insights.so_what: Courts are pushing back on federal prosecutions tied to enforcement surges.
